correctness.rationale: The invariant convex realization and dual-face identification reduce the quotient to a genuine inversion-free barycentric orbit CW chain complex of a six-simplex boundary. The complete certificate verifies exact integral incidence maps, d²=0, Burnside counts, all 1,705 ±1 cancellations and reduced differentials d4=(7,7), d5=(-2,2). Thus H3=Z/7 and H4=Z/2, with no other positive homology; the fixed-reflection Armstrong argument establishes π1 trivial. No homotopy classification is inferred from homology.

value.rationale: The full dihedral quotient of the canonical seven-vertex cyclohedron is a natural nonfree symmetry space, not an arbitrary finite slice. Its rational acyclicity masks two distinct torsion primes in consecutive dimensions, resolving a genuinely integral question not answered by convex geometry or cyclic lens homology. A precise full classification for this exceptional finite case is a useful reference for equivariant graph-associahedron topology.
